source.title: Linear Steerability in Language Models: When It Emerges and How It Evolves
source.authors: Jianshu She; Xinyue Li; E. Xing; Zheng-Zhong Liu; Qi-Rong Ho

page_placements.theme: Distinct capability and intervention timescales in language models

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies when activation-based linear steering becomes effective. It does not test delayed generalization or any of the grokking versions; it cites work on grokking in its references.
record.gate_note: The paper reports delayed emergence of intervention efficacy, including emotion-intensity judgments and reasoning accuracy after activation-vector addition. These are results about induced linear steerability, which the authors distinguish from other model abilities; they do not measure spontaneous delayed generalization. Accordingly, the rows are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"], not as tests of a claim version. The paper also reports ID scores, entropy, cosine similarity, and representation analyses; those are not rows here because they do not measure the behavior named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper studies when activation-steering efficacy emerges across LLM pretraining checkpoints. It deliberately induces behaviour via vector addition and measures steerability, not delayed generalization (train vs. test accuracy) on any task. It cites Nanda et al. 2023 only in related work. It tests no grokking version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that linear steerability develops over training at concept-specific stages, aligned with increasingly linearly separable representations. They present ID metrics (layer differences, entropy, cosine similarity) as heuristic signals of when steering becomes effective. They report the pattern is similar on Amber.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies activation-based steering and its emergence across language-model checkpoints, not the grokking training recipe or delayed-generalization measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences by concept and checkpoint; it also notes that intervention coefficient and layer selection affect outcomes, with best coefficients differing across model families.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation-steering efficacy for emotion concepts appears abruptly late in CrystalCoder pretraining. Anger shows no effect before about 68% of training steps, then a sharp rise. Timing differs by concept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear steerability of concepts in LLMs emerges abruptly at concept-specific stages of pretraining, after the model can already express the concept.

fits_no_version.finding: On four reasoning datasets, steering-vector intervention hurts accuracy at early checkpoints. It surpasses the no-intervention accuracy only late: RACE 90%, OBQA 65%, ARC-C 99%, ARC-E 98% of pretraining.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear intervention efficacy on reasoning benchmarks emerges late in pretraining. Its timing coincides with spikes in inter-layer ID-score differences.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
record.problems: The emotion assessment relies on ChatGPT judgments and the paper acknowledges subjectivity and difficulty determining emergence precisely. It reports only two 7B-scale model families, tunes intervention coefficients empirically, and does not investigate why coefficients differ across models. Several results are conveyed qualitatively or in figures; numerical uncertainty for the intervention outcomes is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: ID scores, entropy, cosine similarity, representation analyses, and the Amber ID heatmaps were not included because they do not measure the delayed-generalization behavior in the claim versions. No result rows were assigned to those analyses.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets, no train/test accuracy gap, no training-set-size manipulation.
No circuit formation, memorization removal, or progress measures anticipating a generalization jump. The ID metrics anticipate steerability, not generalization.
No init-scale or weight-norm manipulation, and no delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data.
Uses LLM pretraining checkpoints but measures steering efficacy, not delayed generalization of held-out performance after training-set fit.
No weight decay, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/cites_only classification is correct; the reference to 2301.05217 appears only in related work. The abrupt late emergence of steerability is superficially grokking-like, but it is an induced intervention effect measured on fixed pretraining checkpoints. There is no train/test generalization gap, so it fits no version. Table 10 also gives spike checkpoints (RACE 93%, OBQA 63%, ARC-C 99%, ARC-E 100%). These are the paper's own heuristic predictor, not claim evidence, and the rows correctly omit them.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test training-versus-test accuracy, overfitting, chance-level test performance, or how delay varies with training-set size.
It analyzes linear representations and steerability, not the formation of a grokking circuit, removal of memorizing components, or anticipation of a generalization jump.
It studies steerability in language-model checkpoints, not grokking-like delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data or switching such delays through initialization scale or weight norm.
The paper examines training checkpoints of language models but does not measure delayed generalization during realistic pretraining or fine-tuning.
It does not test weight decay, low-norm bias, circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
It does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instability, softmax floating-point limits, or whether controls for these remove grokking.

source_check.notes: Each pretraining checkpoint was dialogue-fine-tuned before evaluation (Section 4). Figure 1 reports no notable anger-steering effect before approximately 68%, rather than establishing an exactly zero effect; these are induced steering results.
